title: High-mass star formation at sub-50 au scales
question: What are the physical properties of the densest structures (fragmentation, kinematics, jet/outflow vs disk) in the high-mass hot core G351.77-0.54 at sub-50 au resolution?

data.angular_resolution: 21 mas x 15 mas continuum (PA -74 deg); ~25 x 20 mas lines (PA -86 deg)
data.sensitivity: continuum 1 sigma ~50 uJy/beam; lines ~0.9 mJy/beam per 1 km/s channel

what.value: ATLASGAL 870 um peak flux density 52.1 Jy/beam (19.2'' beam)

evidence.quote: Scaling the 870 $\mu$m peak flux density of 52.1 Jy beam$^{-1}$ (with a beam size of $19.2''$)

what.value: Previous ALMA 690 GHz CO(6-5) and CH3CN data, 438 um continuum sources

evidence.quote: Figure [6](#mom1_co) shows the previous CO(6–5) data (cite: beuther2017b)
we are using for the 1.3 mm dust opacity $\kappa$ a value of 1.11 cm$^2$ g$^{-1}$ from (cite: ossenkopf1994) at high densities of $10^8$ cm$^{-3}$.

recipe.method: ALMA pipeline in CASA, then phase-only self-calibration
Continuum from whole bandpass with robust -2; lines with robust 0; baselines >55 m only

recipe.goal: identify continuum cores and measure fluxes, Tb
recipe.method: identified by eye following 5 sigma contours; integrated fluxes within 4 sigma contours; peak and mean brightness temperatures

recipe.goal: derive masses and column densities (lower limits)
recipe.method: optically thin dust formula with Tb as temperature proxy
key_parameters: column density T = 1000 K for mm1, mm2; 100 K for others; masses use mean Tb within 4 sigma
assumptions: kappa 1.11 cm2/g at 1.3 mm; gas-to-dust 150; distances 1 and 2.2 kpc

recipe.method: Jeans lengths/masses from CORE densities 1e7-1e8 cm-3 and T~50 K compared with observed separations and masses
moment-1 maps, channel maps, position-velocity diagrams of the 217.82 GHz and SiO(5-4) lines; compare to CO(6-5) and CH3CN from earlier data

evidence.quote: This way, we identify 12 separate mm sources within a radius of roughly $3.5''$
the sum of the fluxes of all identified sub-cores accumulates to only $\sim$208 mJy.
we recover only about 2.1% of the total continuum emission in the field.

answer_key.value: 0.01-0.51 Msun at 1 kpc; 0.1-2.5 Msun at 2.2 kpc

evidence.quote: we derive high values for the approximate molecular hydrogen densities around $6.8\times 10^{10}$ cm$^{-3}$.
we find Jeans lengths between roughly 870 and 2800 au

answer_key.quantity: highest velocities in 217.82 GHz moment 1 near mm1

evidence.quote: the highest velocities are close to the center of mm1 with values of +7.9 and $-9.0$ km s$^{-1}$ within a separation of only $\sim$0.01$''$

answer_key.quantity: separation of peaks in -18 and +14 km/s channels

evidence.quote: The spatial peak positions in the channels at $-18$ and +14 km s$^{-1}$ are separated by only $0.049''$ or $\sim$108/49 au
